title: Lab-driven feature experiments roadmap Q4 2028
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines the roadmap, governance model, and operational playbook for Redwood's Lab-Driven Feature Experiments program (the Lab). The Lab is a small-batch, safety-and-cost-aware environment for validating product and runtime changes that impact inference economics, fidelity, and developer ergonomics prior to wider rollout.

Goals

- Accelerate validated learning about feature value and economics using constrained, instrumented experiments.
- Reduce rollout risk for changes that affect cost per token, latency SLOs, or model output fidelity.
- Create repeatable guardrails and telemetry for feature-level decisions (accept, iterate, rollback).

Scope

- In-scope: model variant pilots, quantization profiles, batching and caching policies, routing heuristics, SDK UX changes that affect request surface, and console telemetry experiments.
- Out-of-scope: major infra (fleet resizing), customer-facing billing model changes, and any experiment that requires global data residency changes. Those require separate enterprise review.

Key success metrics (per-experiment)

1) Primary business metric (one only): e.g., increased API conversion or reduced per-token cost for sample workload. Target specified in experiment brief.
2) Performance safety metrics (must not regress):
   - Median tail latency (p95) change <= +10% vs baseline
   - Error rate (5xx/4xx) increase <= 0.5 percentage points absolute
   - KV cache hit rate impact documented if relevant
3) Fidelity safety metrics:
   - BLEU/ROUGE/LLMScore change <= threshold defined per prompt set (default: 2% absolute)
   - Regression alerting bound: any metric drop > 3% triggers immediate pause
4) Cost/Economics:
   - Estimated per-token cost delta documented in experiment brief
   - Burn budget cap enforced (see Cost and resourcing)

Quarterly roadmap (Q4 2028)

- Week 1-3 (Oct): Establish baseline telemetry dashboards and canonical prompt-sets for three product verticals (Search, Automated Support, Content Gen). Owners: Product–Asha, Signals–Sophie.
- Week 4-6 (Nov): Run small-batch quant-fallback experiments (2 model variants * 3 quant profiles) on dedicated lab cluster. Deliverable: per-variant fidelity matrix and cost delta table. Owners: Applied ML–Miguel, Runtime–Raj.
- Week 7-10 (Nov-Dec): SDK surface experiment: streaming chunk sizes and default retry policy change. Canary to 2% of traffic via dev sandbox tokens. Deliverable: conversion vs latency trade-off report. Owners: Developer DX–Kara.
- Week 11-12 (Dec): Governance review, consolidate results, decide promotion candidates for production canary or return to iteration.

Experiment lifecycle and governance

- Proposal: submit an Experiment Brief (single-page) with hypothesis, primary metric, safety criteria, data retention, owners, and budget. Template below.
- Approval: Experiment Review Board (ERB) approves experiments with one of: green (go), conditional (go with guardrails), or deny. ERB membership: Product Lead (chair), Applied ML, Runtime, Security, Finance.
- Run: experiments run on the Lab cluster or sandbox routes depending on risk. All experiments must include automated telemetry and a rollback flag.
- Review: post-run review within 5 business days with artifacts: raw telemetry, analysis notebook, and promotion recommendation.
- Promotion: promotion to production requires an explicit promotion PRD that maps metrics to production SLOs and cost commitments.

Experiment brief template (single page)

- Title
- Owner and team
- Background and hypothesis
- Primary metric and success threshold
- Safety metrics and hard stop thresholds
- Estimated cost delta and burn budget (USD/month or tokens/month)
- Duration and traffic target (sandbox %, reserved pool)
- Data retention and PII considerations
- Rollback criteria and owner contact

Runbook / step-by-step (numbered)

1) Create Experiment Brief and attach canonical prompt set and baseline snapshots.
2) Submit ERB request (email + link) and allow 48 business hours for approval; emergency experiments can request expedited review.
3) Provision lab resources via the Lab provisioning CLI:
   - CLI example: redwood-lab provision --cluster lab-q4-2028 --variant v01 --quant-int8 --budget 5000
4) Deploy experiment and enable telemetry collector with tags: experiment-id, owner, vertical.
5) Monitor dashboards for safety thresholds; on breach, execute: redwood-lab rollback --experiment <id> --reason "safety-threshold-breach"
6) Run until pre-declared minimum sample size or duration achieved.
7) Produce post-run report and present to ERB for promotion decision.

Telemetry and dashboards (minimum required)

- Top-level: primary metric trend, median and p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, KV/cache hit ratio.
- Fidelity: prompt-set-specific scoring charts and confusion breakdowns.
- Economics: estimated per-request cost and projected monthly run-rate.

Cost and resourcing

- Each experiment must declare a hard burn budget. Default sandbox budget: $5k/month. Any experiment expecting > $20k must receive Finance sign-off.
- Lab clusters are billed to an internal cost center; chargeback to product teams occurs monthly.

Architecture / reference configuration (table)

Service | Purpose | Default config | Owner
------- | ------- | -------------- | -----
lab-cluster-q4 | isolated GPU pool for small-batch pilots | 4 x A100-80GB, preemptible | eng-infra
lab-routing-proxy | routes sandbox tokens | rate-limit 100rps | eng-platform
telemetry-collector | ingest and annotate experiment traces | retention 90d, schema v2 | signals
variant-orchestrator | manage model variant routing and fallback | canary 2%, fallback policy: immediate | runtime

Promotion criteria to production canary

- Primary metric meets or exceeds success threshold with 95% confidence.
- No safety metric breaches during full experiment window.
- Performance headroom validated on production-like load (stress test p99 < 1.2x baseline).
- Cost delta within committed commercial bounds.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Unanticipated fidelity regressions in long tail prompts. Mitigation: extended long-tail prompt set run and manual review by Applied ML.
- Risk: Cost overrun. Mitigation: hard burn budget and automated budget-enforcement hooks.
- Risk: Security/data exposure. Mitigation: experiments default to synthetic or scrubbed prompt-sets; PII experiments require Security sign-off.

Appendix: sample experiment config (YAML)

experiment_id: lab-q4-2028-quant-01
owner: asha.patel@redwood.com
variant: gptx-mini-v1
quant_profile: int8-safety-1
traffic_target: 1%
duration_days: 14
burn_budget_usd: 3000
primary_metric: "support-ticket-resolution-rate"
